notes:
Topline: SignalHarbor is a mid-market customer success platform focused on e-mail + ticket automation for retail merchants.
- Primary pain: noisy manual tags, slow triage during spikes (Black Friday volume x6), agents burn out w/ repetitive summaries.
- Desired: automatic concise ticket/email summaries (1-3 bullets), auto-tagging with confidence scores, suggested macros and one-click apply.
- Integration: Zendesk (primary), also Freshdesk evaluation in parallel. Need ability to push tags + add internal notes + trigger macros via API/webhook.
- Throughput targets: avg 200 reqs/min normal, 1200 reqs/min peak; tail latency SLA < 250ms for suggested tag API (95p), summary batching acceptable if sub-1s perceived.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — will accept slightly higher cost for reliable peak handling; looking at reserved capacity for peak windows.
- Model preferences: open-model variants first, but willing to use Redwood curated LLMs. Need deterministic tag rules + fallback to lightweight reranker.
- Security: must support SSO (SAML), audit logs delivered to internal SIEM, customer-managed KMS for keys, option for EU data residency for EU merchants.
- Quote from Head of Ops: "We need tags we can trust — false positives cost ops time and revenue."
- CRM notes: shorthand: POC -> sandbox zendesk, replay historical peak data (Oct-Nov) through Redwood batching; evaluate tagging precision @ different thresholds; measure agent handoff reduction.
- Action items: get Zendesk admin install, legal sign residency addendum, finalize rate-limit/cost model for dedicated burst windows.
- Risk: legal residency timeline could push to Private deployment; this upsells but adds procurement friction.
- Good fit: Redwood's dedicated + smart routing looks like match for predictable peaks and graceful fallback.
timeline_summary: POC scoped mid-Feb -> POC running early March -> legal + Zendesk scopes block full rollout; target pilot close May
